newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends mixed, no effect in Thai news.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends mixed, no effect in Thai news.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended mixed on Friday, with the benchmark RSS1 staying steady while the SMR20 dropped a cent in value.
Dealers said the market was dead and strongly disputed an official trade source's information at midday that a shipment of July SMR20 to Britain was sold at 264 cents a kg.
"To the best of our knowledge, we haven't heard of it," said a dealer with a private rubber broking house. "The market has been dead for the last three days."
The trade source said the British deal was done in early trading and gave some life to an otherwise dead market.
At the close, the July RSS1 buyer was officially quoted at 284 Malaysian/Singapore cents ($1.13) a kg, unchanged from Thursday. July SMR20 buyer was down a cent at 263.
Traders quoted the SMR 20 at 260 cents a kg, SMR CV at 331, SMR L at 308, SMR 10 at 262 and drum latex at 226.
The INRO five-day average was at 216.36 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on June 5 against 216.29 on June 4. The daily indicator was at 215.52 against 216.76.
A shipping agent quoted freight rates for rubber from Malaysia to Rotterdam at $800 per TEU and $1,700 per two-TEU containers.
Dealers also said the market did not react to news that the Bangkok government will spend another billion baht ($40,000) by July to buy rubber in the Thai market.
Chakant Saengraksawong, director of the Hat Yai rubber auction market, said 5,770 tonnes of rubber had been bought under government intervention since May 15.
"It's no big news to us...the market has discounted it," said a dealer.
"What is the Thai government going to do with all this rubber, who are they going to sell it to when we traders ourselves have problems? That we'd like to know," added the trader.
Dealers said trading price of both the RSS1 and SMR20 were likely to fall by a half to one cent daily for next week if sentiment did not improve.
